newsitem.title: ITALY: SWIMMING-ANOTHER WORLD RECORD FOR PANKRATOV. [CORRECTED 21:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-ANOTHER WORLD RECORD FOR PANKRATOV. [CORRECTED 21:50 GMT]

text.p: Double Olympic champion Denis Pankratov, denied by an organisational blunder in Paris a year ago, broke his second short-course world swimming record in less than a week on Wednesday.

Pankratov clocked 51.93 seconds in the 100 metres butterfly on the second day of a World Cup meeting, beating Canadian Marcel Gery's world mark of 52.07, set in Leicester, England, on February 23, 1990.

The Russian beat both the 100 and 200 butterfly world short-course marks in Paris last year only to be denied the records because French meet organisers had run out of bottles to administer the dope tests necessary for ratification.

Pankratov, who won both 100 and 200 butterfly Olympic titles in Atlanta last year, finally claimed the 200 butterfly short-course world record with a time of 1:52.64 at a World Cup meeting in Gelsenkirchen, Germany, last Saturday.
He is the first man to hold all four butterfly world records -- 100 and 200 long-course (50-metre pool) and short-course (25-metre pool) -- since the great Michael Gross.
The Imperia meeting was the seventh of the eight-venue World Cup series which ends in Paris next weekend.
"What can I say? The race speaks for itself," said Pankratov, whose compatriot Konstantin Ushkov set the early pace.
"My friend Ushkov was swimming fast -- he was first after 50 metres -- so I just had to swim faster," Pankratov said.
Ukraine's Denis Silantiev finished second in 52.19, with Ushkov third in 52.49. Both Pankratov and Silantiev were inside the 52.26 European mark Ushkov set in Gelsenkirchen last Sunday.
Almost exactly a year ago Pankratov clocked 51.94 in the 100 butterfly and 1:52.34 in the 200 butterfly at the Paris World Cup meeting where the dope test fiasco occurred.

China's Le Jingyi gained revenge over fellow Olympic gold medallist Claudia Poll in her speciality 100 metres freestyle after finishing third behind her Costa Rican rival in the 200 freestyle, Poll's speciality, on Tuesday.
Le clocked 54.88 seconds, outside her world record 53.01 (corrects from 24.23), to finish ahead of Poll (55.00) and Leah Martindale of Barbados (55.73).
Poll gained consolation by winning the gold in the 400 metres freestyle, clocking 4:08.18 to beat Japan's Eri Yamanoi and Kirsten Vlieghuis of the Netherlands.
Poll also won the 800 metres freestyle on Tuesday.
Cai Huijue of China came close to a women's 50 butterfly world record, winning in 26.68 seconds, 0.12 seconds outside the world mark of Australia's Angie Kennedy.

It was also a victorious day for British swimmers, with former world short-course champion Mark Foster winning the men's 50 metres freestyle in 22.14 and Susan Rolph taking the 100 metres individual medley in 1:02.00.
"I've had three weeks of hard training," Foster said. "Now I think I'll be ready to take the world record back from Alex (Russian Olympic champion Alexander Popov). That's the aim."
